title: Abundance for All: where the gaps are today

needs.stat_text: 8.5% of the world's people were undernourished in 2023.
needs.licence: CC BY 4.0 (World Bank, World Development Indicators)
needs.could_change: We believe robots that plant, tend and harvest, guided by a superintelligence that learns every field, could help every harvest reach every table.

needs.stat_text: 73.7% of people used safely managed drinking water in 2024. About one person in four did not.
needs.licence: CC BY 4.0 (World Bank, World Development Indicators)
needs.underlying_source: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme, via World Bank WDI
needs.gap: People using safely managed drinking water services
needs.could_change: We believe tireless machines and smarter engineering could build, repair and watch over the pipes, pumps and treatment plants that safe water depends on.

needs.stat_text: 23.2% of the world's urban population lived in slums in 2022.
needs.licence: CC BY 4.0 (World Bank, World Development Indicators)
needs.underlying_source: UN-Habitat Urban Indicators Database, via World Bank WDI
needs.could_change: We believe robot builders and AI design could make a safe, good home something that can be built quickly, to a standard, for anyone.

needs.stat_text: The world's under-5 mortality rate was 37.4 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2024.
needs.licence: CC BY 4.0 (World Bank, World Development Indicators)
needs.underlying_source: UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation, via World Bank WDI
needs.could_change: We believe AI could bring the knowing how of the best doctor to every clinic, and speed up the medicines and vaccines that protect children.

needs.stat_text: 91.9% of people had access to electricity in 2024. The rest, about 8%, did not.
needs.licence: CC BY 4.0 (World Bank, World Development Indicators)
needs.underlying_source: SDG 7.1.1 Electrification Dataset (Tracking SDG7), via World Bank WDI
needs.could_change: We believe robots could build and maintain clean power at a scale people alone cannot, and AI could run the grids that carry it.

needs.stat_text: 48.3% of children at the end of primary-school age were below minimum reading proficiency in 2019 (learning poverty).
needs.licence: CC BY 4.0 (World Bank, World Development Indicators)
needs.underlying_source: World Bank / UNESCO Institute for Statistics (learning poverty), via World Bank WDI
needs.gap: Learning poverty, adjusted for out-of-school children
needs.could_change: We believe a patient AI tutor in every child's own language could be there for every learner, wherever the nearest school is.

ingredients.label: Robotics
ingredients.stat_text: The world's factories now run a record 5 million industrial robots, up 9% in 2025.
ingredients.licence: Quoted fact from an IFR press release (Sep 24, 2026); © IFR, linked and attributed, not reproduced

ingredients.label: Clean energy
ingredients.stat_text: Solar produced 8.7% of the world's electricity in 2025.
ingredients.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Ember; shown via Our World in Data)

ingredients.label: Superintelligence
ingredients.stat_text: An AI system's predicted protein structures are now free to every scientist: over 200 million of them.
ingredients.licence: CC BY 4.0 (EMBL-EBI AlphaFold Protein Structure Database)
ingredients.note: The page states 'over 200 million'; year is the retrieval year because the page itself carries no date.

dropped.figure: Number of people without electricity access
dropped.reason: No open headcount series was found at the source; the World Bank share (91.9%) is used instead. A headcount obtained by multiplying by population would be a derived number, so it is not shown.
